# Sprint plan — Events as composition substrate — durable delivery on a verified core, with the human surface in the loop

*v3, revised 2026-07-05 after external review of v2. v1–v2 generated by the
`sprint-plan` workflow (19 agents); the workflow transcripts, candidate
analysis, and both rounds of review feedback live in
[sprint-2026-07-05-provenance.md](sprint-2026-07-05-provenance.md).
v3 changes: explicit Sprint A / Sprint B split, Phase 1 un-bundled, the /ui
render pulled to day one, the dogfood time-boxed, a two-part pre-registered
gate, reject-at-registration as the RFC default, appendices moved out.*

**Verdict:** the log is now provably crash-safe (foundation gate), but neither
the real external dogfood nor the synthetic sweep found a relied-upon consumer
losing events that matter — the friction was the interaction contract, not
durable delivery. **Sprint B (outbox + webhooks) is deferred**, not cancelled;
the RFC captures the full design, ready if a real go signal arrives. The verdict
is a recommendation for the maintainer to confirm.

Open handoffs (see [HANDOVER-2026-07-06.md](HANDOVER-2026-07-06.md)): publish
the first release (v0.1.0), and confirm/override the no-go.

## Theme

The events engine is built through Step 3 but its payoff is unproven, and review verified the plan's original foundation story was partly stale: ClaimAtomic is already fixed at HEAD, while the real log-integrity gap is fireOne's mark-then-append crash window — which would silently defeat the outbox on the exact path it demos. **Sprint A** verifies-then-hardens the actual gaps, ships the attachments evidence loop end-to-end starting with the /ui surface humans actually look at, dogfoods the real board (web UI included) to produce a pre-registered two-part gate verdict, and closes with the Subscriber RFC written cold. **Sprint B** — outbox + webhooks — is a separate, gated commitment: it happens only on a "go" verdict and an agreed RFC, and cutting it is the planned response to a "no-go," not a failure. Value curve stated honestly: the hardening phases are insurance (their demos show concretely averted loss); the render, attachments, and dogfood phases are visible value for humans, operators, and integrators. The hard line holds: conditions only ever emit — the core never acts.

**North star:** Convert the events investment from a potential in-core engine into the composition substrate the philosophy demands: land Step 4 (durable outbox/tailer) and then the webhook delivery kind, so the completed condition-events machinery becomes something external processes consume — not something the core acts on. This is the single most vision-advancing direction because it is the direct test of 'small core, big composition' and 'hooks, not engines': it makes the largest existing investment pay off for the USER (reliable, replayable reactive coordination instead of drop-on-crash SSE) while keeping all reaction outside the core. Do it in parallel with the low-risk, high-leverage attachments wiring (a kept-small core capability that is fully built but dark), and hold the line that conditions only ever emit — they never mutate.

### Phase A3 — fireOne atomicity fix *(M, the one risky item — own room, own demo)*

**Goal:** Close the real log-integrity gap: MarkConditionFired and the durable event append commit in **separate** transactions (monitor.go:340 marks, append follows), so a crash between them permanently loses the event AND suppresses re-fire — unrecoverable by any later cursor replay, and upstream of any outbox. The append-then-mark vs single-tx choice affects re-fire semantics under crash and is settled here, not discovered in review. Fix the adjacent swallowed errors (DEBT-06 SSE replay, DEBT-07 PutIdempotency) here too, so they don't ride a gated sprint. Beneficiary: operator — insurance, framed as averted loss.

| Do | Outcome (acceptance) | Likely files |
|---|---|---|
| Make mark+append one transaction for persist:true conditions (or append-then-mark with idempotent replay); decide and document the crash re-fire semantics. | A forced crash between verify and dispatch can no longer strand a fired-but-never-appended condition; a fault-injection test proves the marks row and log row commit together. | internal/core/monitor.go fireOne, internal/core/events.go, internal/sqlite/sqlite.go (condition_marks tx) |
| Surface DEBT-06 (swallowed SSE replay error) and DEBT-07 (swallowed PutIdempotency) instead of dropping them. | Both error paths are visible in logs/responses; tests cover each. | internal/httpapi/sse.go, internal/httpapi/middleware.go |

**Demo:** trigger a persist:true condition, kill the process in the old mark-then-append window, restart — under the old code the escalation is gone forever with no trace and never re-fires; under the new code it either never marked or is in the log. 'Here is the alert you would silently never have received.' This fault-injection test is also the **foundation gate** of A7.

**Exit:** mark+append atomic with a crash-window fault-injection test; DEBT-06/07 fixed; suite green.

**Goal:** serve.go already cancels the supervisor ctx on ListenAndServe exit, but cancellation is fire-and-forget — no WaitGroup/drain, so shutdown doesn't await goroutine exit or in-flight hook spawns. Establish the ctx + WaitGroup + bounded-drain-timeout pattern once, documented as the template the Sprint B tailer and webhook worker must reuse.

### Phase A7 — Dogfood session, time-boxed → gate verdict

**Goal:** Run the daily loop through ALL surfaces — /ui board and card detail, CLI, MCP take_next/append_entry, attach a real build log (A5) and see it on the card page — keeping a friction log that covers the web experience, not just terminal ergonomics. **Time-box: one working session.** Exit is the recorded verdict, not exhaustion of findings. Beneficiary: the maintaining team as real users.

**Depends on:** A2, A5, A6.

**The gate (pre-registered in docs/design/OUTBOX-GONOGO.md BEFORE the session starts, two parts):**

1. **Foundation gate — binary, must pass.** The A3 fault-injection test: fire ≥N persist:true condition events during the session, induce one SIGKILL in the old crash window, restart, diff the event log against the set of fired conditions. **Any fired condition absent from the log ⇒ automatic no-go** — the log itself is not trustworthy and Sprint B has no foundation; fix A3 before anything else.
2. **Needs gate — decides whether Sprint B is built.** Pitched at the *delivery* layer, where the residual gap actually lives once A3 makes the log crash-safe: during real use, kill -9 mid-dispatch and record whether any consumer the team relies on (shell hook — at-most-once; a disconnected SSE client without replay) missed an event that IS in the log, and whether that miss mattered to anyone. **Go ⇔ a relied-upon consumer demonstrably missed (or would have missed) events the log retained. No-go ⇔ no delivery gap was hit or mattered** — then Sprint B is cut and re-planned, and the RFC (A8) still lands.

| Do | Outcome (acceptance) | Likely files |
|---|---|---|
| Write OUTBOX-GONOGO.md with both criteria BEFORE dogfooding; run the session through web + CLI + MCP; conclude with the recorded verdict. | A friction log spanning web + CLI + MCP; review-notify fired on genuine transitions; both gate results recorded against the pre-registered criteria, with board screenshots as evidence alongside the committed JSONL. | examples/demo-workspace (live board), internal/httpapi/ui (exercised), internal/mcp (exercised), internal/hooks (review-notify in anger), docs/design/OUTBOX-GONOGO.md (criteria + verdict) |

**Demo:** Live-drive the maintainers' backlog on the actual /ui board: MCP take_next claims the next real card, the column updates live in the browser, attach a build log and see it render on card detail, transition and watch review-notify fire. Close by reading out both gate results.

**Exit:** friction log covering the human surface; OUTBOX-GONOGO.md with pre-registered criteria and a recorded two-part verdict; no new endpoints/fields/event types added.

### Phase A8 — SUBSCRIBERS.md RFC *(paper; parallel with A7; Sprint A's final deliverable)*

**Goal:** Design once, on paper, cold — while there is no coding pressure — the three things that are design failures if drifted into: (1) the name collision — core.Subscriber (bus.go:51) is an ephemeral in-process listener with no cursor, a different species from the durable entity; (2) ephemeral-condition deliverability — condition events default to the Signal path and never enter the log, so a durable consumer's filter is silently a no-op for half the catalog; (3) dispatch topology — Emit already publishes synchronously to bus/observers, so a tailer that 'republishes' double-delivers. The RFC lands regardless of the gate verdict. It needs only verified codebase facts (available now), not the friction log — so it runs in parallel with A7.

| Do | Outcome (acceptance) | Likely files |
|---|---|---|
| Write docs/design/SUBSCRIBERS.md resolving, before any code: **naming** (rename the durable entity — e.g. Consumer — or the bus struct, with an explicit mapping from ephemeral core.Subscriber to the durable model); **per-type deliverability** — the default answer is **reject-at-registration**: registering a durable consumer for an ephemeral condition type is rejected with a clear error, and EVENTS.md gains a versioned per-type durable/ephemeral column; auto-escalation to persist:true is specified only as a possible future extension, because it would mutate the startup-only PersistConditions invariant at runtime and re-arm MonitorScheduler (IsPersisted) — a known-gnarly path this RFC declines by default; **dispatch topology** (tailer feeds only new durable consumers, bus/observers stay synchronous — or replaces sync dispatch, re-specifying the observer/hook synchrony contract); where durable interest is computed for MonitorScheduler so liveness has one owner; the hooks-migration and static-vs-runtime forks; auth/SSRF for /v1/subscribers; migration ordering relative to migrateEventsScope's table rebuild using the existing idempotent-DDL pattern; and deterministic fake-clock injection (internal/core/clocktest) as a requirement for retry/backoff tests. | One agreed model answering naming, deliverability (reject-at-registration default), topology, liveness ownership, hooks fork, auth/SSRF, migrations, and testability — reviewed cold before any Sprint B code. | docs/design/SUBSCRIBERS.md (new), docs/events/EVENTS.md §8/§9/§12 |

**Exit (= Sprint A complete):** RFC agreed; both gate verdicts recorded; A1–A6 landed; suite green; origin == local.

# Sprint B — durable outbox + webhooks *(separate sprint; gated)*

**Entry criteria — all three, or Sprint B does not start:** (1) A7 foundation gate passed; (2) A7 needs gate verdict is "go"; (3) SUBSCRIBERS.md agreed. On a no-go, this section is re-planned from the friction log — cutting it is the planned response, not a failure.

### Phase B1 — Durable cursor + tailer + dead-letter

**Goal:** At-least-once delivery across restart, built on the A3-hardened log and the A4 drain convention, per the RFC's topology. Beneficiary: operator/integrator — insurance, demoed as averted loss.

| Do | Outcome (acceptance) | Likely files |
|---|---|---|
| Implement the durable per-consumer cursor + background tailer reading the events table in id order, feeding durable consumers only per the RFC's topology (no double-delivery to existing bus subscribers), plus dead-letter records — with fake-clock-driven backoff tests. | A consumer with a stored cursor disconnects, the server restarts, and on reconnect it receives every missed event in order at-least-once per the RFC; existing bus/SSE subscribers receive each event exactly as often as before (regression-tested); tailer drains cleanly on shutdown. | internal/core/events.go, bus.go, internal/sqlite/sqlite.go (cursor + dead-letter tables), internal/core tailer |
| Unify consumer liveness per the RFC so MonitorScheduler treats a disconnected-but-behind durable cursor as still interested; add regression coverage for what the async path could visibly break: temporal_test.go exact-timing assertions AND an integration check that the live /ui board's EventSource-driven re-render still receives mutation events correctly ordered under the tailer. | Temporal conditions stay armed for behind-but-durable consumers; temporal and SSE timing tests pass; the human live board demonstrably still updates in order — no stale columns or missed re-renders. | internal/core/monitor.go, bus.go, service.go wiring, internal/httpapi tests (EventSource/board SSE integration) |

**Demo:** Register a durable consumer, generate a breach + card_idle, kill -9 mid-dispatch, restart: the consumer replays from its cursor and receives everything it would previously have lost — including a duplicate-delivery segment showing consumers deduping by event id, so at-least-once is demonstrated honestly. Side-by-side, the /ui board keeps re-rendering live and in order.

**Exit:** at-least-once delivery across restart via stored cursors with dead-letter and clean drain; no double-delivery to pre-existing bus consumers; duplicate-delivery (dedupe-by-event-id across mid-dispatch kill) covered by a regression test, not a doc footnote; temporal/SSE timing tests and the /ui live-board integration check pass; EVENTS.md records commit-vs-dispatch decoupling as a versioned contract.

### Phase B2 — Webhook delivery kind and /v1/subscribers with enforced egress allowlist

**Goal:** The composition payoff: conditions delivered outward to independent processes via durable, retryable webhooks, with reaction entirely outside the core. Runtime registration of arbitrary outbound URLs is the first runtime-mutable extension-like entity in a file-declared system, so the SSRF control is an enforced default-deny egress allowlist shipped WITH the surface — a documented assumption is not a control. If the allowlist can't land, webhook subscribers stay file-declared this sprint. Beneficiary: external integrator + operator.

**Depends on:** B1.

| Do | Outcome (acceptance) | Likely files |
|---|---|---|
| Implement the webhook delivery kind as a tailer consumer per the RFC: at-least-once with retry/backoff (fake-clock tested), HMAC-signed payloads, per-subscriber dead-letter — reusing the A4 drain and B1 cursor conventions. Deliverability per the RFC: subscribing to an ephemeral condition type is rejected at registration, never a silent no-op. | status_timeout fires an HMAC-signed POST to a local endpoint; a flaky endpoint is retried then dead-lettered; delivery survives restart via the cursor; an ephemeral-type subscription is rejected with a clear error. | internal/config/extensions.go (Extension/HookFilter), internal/core (tailer consumer), internal/sqlite (subscriptions table) |
| Add /v1/subscribers (create/list/status/delete) reusing withActor/idempotent middleware, exposing delivery attempts, retry counts, last error, and dead-letter state — with an ENFORCED default-deny outbound host/CIDR allowlist (config-declared) validated at registration and at dispatch. JSON-only operator surface this sprint: the /ui health view is explicitly recorded as an accepted gap with a follow-up card. | GET /v1/subscribers shows cursor and delivery health; registering a URL outside the allowlist is rejected with a clear error; a dispatch-time allowlist re-check blocks DNS-swap tricks; the no-UI gap is a tracked card, not an implicit hole. | internal/httpapi/server.go, api.go, middleware.go, internal/config (egress allowlist), internal/sqlite (delivery-attempt queries) |
| Complete EVENTS.md §9's delivery taxonomy (at-least-once push webhooks vs at-most-once shell hooks vs pull-based idempotent SSE/feed) and reconcile §8.6 escalation restart duplication with webhook retries: integrators must dedupe by event id, with the compounding case documented and pointed at the B1 dedupe regression test. | A versioned contract table an outside integrator can build against, including per-type deliverability and duplicate expectations. | docs/events/EVENTS.md §8/§9, docs/events/INTEGRATION.md |

**Demo:** Wire a webhook subscriber to a throwaway chat endpoint, let a card go idle past threshold, and watch the condition arrive HMAC-signed in the external tool with zero reaction logic in the core; kill the endpoint, show retries then dead-lettering in /v1/subscribers, revive it, watch delivery resume from the cursor; then try to register an off-allowlist URL and watch it refused.

**Exit:** webhooks deliver at-least-once with retry/backoff, HMAC, dead-letter, surviving restart; /v1/subscribers ships with an enforced default-deny egress allowlist (registration + dispatch time), or runtime registration is withheld and subscribers stay file-declared; EVENTS.md §9 taxonomy complete; core still only emits — no condition triggers an in-core mutation; operator-UI gap tracked as a card; suite green.

---

## Risks
- The fireOne atomicity fix (A3) touches the hottest reactive path; append-then-mark vs single-tx choice affects re-fire semantics under crash and must be settled in A3, not discovered in review — it is deliberately the only M-with-risk item in Sprint A
- Dispatch topology is the sharpest RFC edge: 'tailer feeds only new durable consumers' preserves the observer synchrony contract but permanently forks two delivery paths; 'tailer replaces sync dispatch' unifies but changes hook timing and SSE latency that tests and the live /ui board assert on — either way the /ui EventSource integration check is the canary
- The needs gate can be gamed toward "go" by contriving a crash nobody would hit; the criterion's "and whether that miss mattered to anyone" clause plus the friction-log requirement are the honesty check — the verdict must cite real-session evidence
- Dogfooding can be gamed by committing one snapshot; the CI doc-id check plus the requirement that the friction log cover the web surface are the acceptance gates
- The egress allowlist is dispatch-time as well as registration-time or it is theater (DNS rebinding); if enforcing that slips, the fallback is file-declared webhook subscribers, already specified in B2
- Engine-creep watch continues: reviewers should reject any PR where a condition performs an in-core write

## Out of scope
- Authentication/identity and permissions as core features — auth stays a host/proxy/extension concern; Sprint B ships the enforced egress allowlist and the RFC's auth/SSRF note, not an in-core authz gate
- Any in-core reaction to conditions — conditions only ever emit; the moment the core acts on one it becomes the workflow-automation platform it disclaims
- Events Step 4+ beyond outbox/webhooks — no projection/job system, no cross-process broker ambitions
- Auto-escalation of ephemeral condition types at subscriber registration — declined as the RFC default (runtime mutation of the startup-only PersistConditions invariant + scheduler re-arm); reject-at-registration ships, auto-escalation is a specified-only future extension
- Bidirectional git-backed mirror / version-gated PATCH-import (NOTES D13) — A6 is strictly one-way export-as-source-of-truth
- Exporting/round-tripping the event journal in JSONL — declined in favor of explicit state-ownership scoping; history/delivery state has one authoritative home (SQLite) and a portable event-log format is a project of its own
- A /ui operator view for subscriber/delivery/dead-letter health — accepted as JSON-only in Sprint B, tracked as a follow-up card (the breaches-page pattern makes it cheap later; B2 is already L-sized)
- Extending the A6 CI check to verify DEBT ledger line:number references against code — the doc short-id check plus the A1 verified reconciliation captures most of the value; full ledger-drift automation is deferred as low value-per-effort
- Migrating the hook Supervisor onto durable cursors unless the RFC explicitly decides to
- Alternative storage backends (Postgres) and a backend-neutral filter AST
- GH-PAGES-TODO docs site + Obsidian/Jira/GitHub ETL — if ever built, an external webhook subscriber, never a core feature
